summary: uv creates the project, the virtual environment and the dependency lock file in one tool. A src-layout keeps your package importable only when installed, which catches path bugs early. pyproject.toml is the single file that describes your project.
goal: Create a Python project with uv, add a typed module, run it, and make your first Git commit.

items.text: Read the Day 2 lesson and answer the two warm-up questions from memory
Step 1: create the project with uv init --package --lib, then run the import check (imported ok)
Step 2: add documents.py, predict preview(d, 3), then run it
Step 3: cause a ModuleNotFoundError on purpose and read the message
Step 4: write reading_minutes and test it (400 words gives 2.0)
Make your first Git commit and add a Status line to the README
Play the Project Doctor game to the end and see your score
